EVALUATION OF ECONOMIC EVIDENCE:
Our examination of the relevant economic evidence will proceed along the following three successive lines of inquiry: (1) has there been a locational shift in urban area economic and social activity? (2) if the evidence demonstrates a significant upswing in the level of suburban economic activity, is there a sufficient nexus between central city and suburban economic activity to suggest that they are commercially interrelated? and (3) if the above two questions are answered in the affirmative, what are the geographic limits of present day commercial areas? Our task is to answer these questions to the best of our ability based on an objective analysis of the available economic data. The ultimate objective of this investigation is to determine if the present population-mileage formula accurately describes the area of business and industrial activity existing about modern-day municipalities.
At the outset of this evaluation of the economic data, a few brief comments are appropriate to dispel certain misconceptions displayed by certain parties in their written representations. This rulemaking proceeding, which was instituted on our own motion pursuant to our authority under section 204(a)(6), is quasi-legislative rather than adjudicative in nature. Notwithstanding contentions to the contrary, there is no burden of proof requirement imposed on any of the participating parties or this Commission.
